subject: Service commitment phasing proposal and remedy split
messages:
From: Liam O'Reilly <liam.oreilly@stratusbank.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: SLA commitments for upcoming Prod launch

Rachel,

Thanks for taking this. We're finalizing the go-live plan for our EU payments stack (targeting mid-May) and have a couple of asks on the SLA side before procurement will sign off. Short version: StratusBank needs a temporary allowance for a lower uptime % during the first 90 days of ramp (regional infra + data residency work), and we want clarity on monthly service credits and a firm cap.

High-level asks: 
- Initial 90-day ramp: allow a temporary uptime baseline of 99.80% (vs your standard 99.95%).
- Monthly remedy: we prefer a pro-rated credit schedule but with an absolute cap equal to one month's committed spend.
- Measurement: we need an EU-region-specific availability metric and monthly report exported in CSV for our audit team.

Can Redwood propose formal amendment language and a capped credit schedule? If helpful, I can share our spend numbers and traffic profile.

Thanks,
Liam
Operations Manager
StratusBank

Attachment: StratusBank-SLA-requests.xlsx (spreadsheet summary of preferred credit curves and traffic ramp)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Reilly <liam.oreilly@stratusbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SLA commitments for upcoming Prod launch

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear outline. Wanted to loop in Marissa (legal) and Ben (AM) so we can put firm language and a commercial compromise on paper.

Quick reactions:
- Redwood standard hosted SLA is 99.95% monthly uptime with a graduated credit ladder.
- We can accommodate a phased ramp for the first 90 days, but we need to be explicit about measurement windows, maintenance carveouts, and a limit on aggregated exposure over the ramp period.
- For the EU-region metric: we can export the monthly availability CSV and include per-route token-level breakdowns (that should satisfy audit).

Request to you: please confirm committed monthly spend for the first 3 months and confirm if the cap you propose should be applied only during the ramp or to all months while the account is active.

Marissa — can you draft a redline for a 90-day amendment that: 1) lowers the baseline to 99.80% for the first 90 days, 2) defines the credit ladder for that period, and 3) limits total credits to a fixed cap (we should propose a conservative percentage if they don't want fixed spend numbers disclosed).

Ben — happy to coordinate approvals and get an exec sign-off if the cap is outside standard commercial playbooks.

Talk soon,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Liam O'Reilly <liam.oreilly@stratusbank.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 15:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SLA commitments for upcoming Prod launch — draft amendment

Liam / team — attaching a draft (redwood-sla-draft-v2.pdf) with language you can review. Key items we included: 

1) Phased baseline:
   - First 90 days from prod_start_date: monthly uptime baseline = 99.80%.
   - After day 90, baseline reverts to 99.95% unless both parties agree to extend in writing.
2) Remedy schedule (ramp period):
   - 99.80% — 99.50%: 5% credit of monthly invoice
   - 99.49% — 99.00%: 10% credit
   - <99.00%: 20% credit
3) Remedy schedule (post-ramp standard): use Redwood standard ladder (graduated credits up to 50%).
4) Cap and aggregation: aggregate credits during first 90 days capped at 20% of the total monthly invoiced amount for that period (we can adjust if you share spend).
5) Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance (48h advance notice) and force majeure excluded.
6) Measurement and reporting: Redwood will produce a region-specific availability CSV with per-route uptime and per-token metrics at month close; disputes to be raised within 30 days.

Notes and open items:
- Liam asked for a cap equal to one month's spend; our proposal above is a 20% cap unless the customer shares committed spend to substantiate a higher cap.
- We need to be explicit on how partial-month prorations are calculated during ramp and any billing credits; suggest referencing our billing appendix.

Please review the draft and call out items to redline. Liam — if you can share the committed spend for months 1–3 we can compute a concrete dollar cap.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-sla-draft-v2.pdf (SLA amendment redline, 6 pages)
From: Liam O'Reilly <liam.oreilly@stratusbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:45:00 +0100
Subject: Re: SLA commitments for upcoming Prod launch — draft amendment

Marissa, Rachel,

Thanks for the thorough draft. A couple of points from procurement:
- We appreciate the ramp ladder, but we cannot accept an uncapped exposure that materially exceeds our risk tolerance. Our request for "cap = one month's committed spend" is intended to be simple and absolute.
- We will share committed spend for months 1–3 (approx. €180k, €240k, €300k) but procurement prefers the cap to be expressed as a multiple of that (1x) rather than a percentage.
- Measurement acceptance: the CSV export is fine, but we need a short self-service endpoint or SFTP export (daily) during the first 90 days for our ops team to validate availability in near-real-time.

I'll upload the spend/traffic file to the link you provided in the spreadsheet. If Redwood can match the 1x cap (one month) limited to the ramp period, we can move forward quickly.

Regards,
Liam

Attachment: StratusBank-SLA-requests.xlsx (updated with spend figures)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Reilly <liam.oreilly@stratusbank.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 11:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SLA commitments for upcoming Prod launch — commercial compromise

Liam — appreciate the clarity and the spend numbers. After a quick review with finance, here's a commercial compromise designed to limit Redwood's exposure while giving Stratus the operational buffer you need: 

Proposal: 
- Ramp window: first 90 days from prod_start_date. Baseline: 99.80%.
- Ramp remedy ladder: Marissa's ladder applies, but aggregate credits during ramp are capped at the lesser of: (a) 1x the monthly committed spend for the applicable month OR (b) 20% of the monthly invoice. Practically, since your month 1 spend (~€180k) gives 1x = €180k, the cap becomes €180k for that month.
- Export: Redwood will provide a daily SFTP export for EU-region availability during the ramp with same CSV columns as monthly report.
- Post-ramp: standard 99.95% baseline and Redwood standard remedy ladder and caps.

I attached a simple visualization (proposed-remedy-chart.png) to show how the cap and ladder interact across the ramp. Next steps: 
1) Marissa to update the redline to reflect the conditional cap language (lesser of 1x committed month OR 20%).
2) Rachel to circulate the amendment for signature once redline is agreed.
3) If approved, Ben will request an exec waiver for the 1x concession (this is extraordinary but doable given strategic nature of the account).

If that's acceptable, can you confirm by EOD Monday 26 Apr?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-remedy-chart.png (PNG, 800x400)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Reilly <liam.oreilly@stratusbank.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 10:00:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SLA commitments for upcoming Prod launch — final amendment and next steps

Liam — looping back with the agreed amendment language and next steps so there's no ambiguity. Per Ben and Marissa's notes, Redwood will: 

- Apply a 90-day phased baseline at 99.80%.
- Use the ramp remedy ladder as drafted by Marissa.
- Cap aggregate credits during each ramp month at the lesser of (a) one times the committed monthly spend for that calendar month, or (b) 20% of the monthly invoice.
- Deliver a daily SFTP export for EU-region availability and the standard monthly CSV report at month close. Disputes to be raised within 30 days.

Next steps: 
1) Marissa to attach the final redline in DocuSign (I will upload within one business day).
2) Liam to confirm the prod_start_date in writing and sign the amendment via DocuSign.
3) Ben to coordinate exec waiver approval paperwork concurrently.

If I don't hear objections by EOD tomorrow we'll route the DocuSign amendment. Thanks for the quick turnaround — excited to get StratusBank live.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference

DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/rooms/xx-abcdef
